title: What If the Indian Monsoon Failed?

scenes.text: What if India's monsoon failed? About 80 percent of the country's rain arrives in one season.
About 60 percent of Indian farming is rain-fed. Fields wait for those clouds.
When it failed in 2002, rainfall ran 19 percent below normal and about 24 million tonnes of grain were lost.
In 2009, the deficit passed 20 percent and 171 districts were declared drought-affected.
Paddy planting dropped by 6 million hectares that year, a quarter less than before.
India held huge grain stocks to cushion those droughts. A total failure would test every reserve.

description:
What if the Indian monsoon failed?
About 80 percent of India's rain comes in one season, and weak monsoons have already cost millions of tonnes of grain.
